1.

The present revision under Section 397 and 399 Cr.PC filed by the revisionist assails the order dated 17.10.2017 in Cr. Case no. 273/1/2014 87045/2016 u/s. 380/406/448 read with section 120-B IPC (hereinafter referred to as "the impugned order") passed by Ld. MM-09, South East District,
Saket Courts, Delhi.
GROUNDS OF REVISION:-
2. The impugned order has been challenged on the grounds that Ld. MM failed to appreciate the contents of complaint in which the complainant specifically stated that accused persons had State vs Manender Pal Singh on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178336647/
1 forcefully demolished the wall between flat No. G-12 & G-13 and stolen the articles which were lying in G-12 i.e. office of residential association; that the Ld. MM has failed to appreciate the contents of statement recorded u/s 161 Cr.PC of public witnesses namely Sh. Madan Lal Garg, Sh. Y. K.
Chaudhary, Sh. K. C. Pahwa, Chaudhary S. Kumar and Sh. Kamaljeet Singh who corroborated the version of complainant and stated that accused persons had forcefully demolished the wall between flat no. G-12 and G-13 and stolen the articles which were lying in G-12 i.e. office of residential association (Ajit Singh house, Yusuf Sarai Commercial Complex Flat owner and occupants association); that the Ld. MM has failed to appreciate the fact that the complainant and public witnesses clearly stated the role attributed to the accused persons in their respective statements;
that Ld. MM has failed to appreciate the fact that at the stage of charge no roving inquiry of the case is required and court should not consider the evidences on record minutely.
In view of the same, it has been prayed the order dated 17.10.2017 passed by Ld. MM be set aside.

sentences.text: Notice of the revision petition was issued to the respondents.
However, no reply was filed on their behalf.
4. The Trial Court record was summoned and perused.
I have heard counsels for both the parties and perused the record.
5. The present revision petition has been filed against the impugned order dated 17.10.2017 whereby the accused persons i.e. respondents were discharged of the offences u/s 380/406/420/448/120B IPC.

A complaint dated 15.02.2001 was made to the concerned police station by Smt. Meera Prasad on behalf of Flat Owners & Occupant Association wherein it was alleged that their office was situated at G-12, ground floor which was taken by Shri Tejwant Singh i.e. respondent no. 2 herein by the President and Treasurar of their Association.
In that office, they had two tables, five chairs, one typewriter and other precious documents of the Association which was used to be locked after the office hours.

On 03.01.2001 when Smt. Meera Prasad, President, Shri Y.K. Chaudhary, Secretary,
Shri Mandan Lal, Member, Shri S.C. Pahwa, Member and Chaudhary S. Kumar, Member came to the office for meeting, they found that the lock of their office was broken and all the said things were missing.
It was also found that the wall between their office at G-12 and flat no. G-13 was demolished and the matter was reported to the police.

They found that Treasurer Shri M.P. Singh rented out his flat bearing no. G-13 to one Shri Kamaljeet Singh in conspiracy with Shri Tejwant Singh and master Prabsaran Singh through their guardian Shri Prabjeet Singh and changed the number of office to G-12 to G-12A.
Not only that respondent no. 2 Shri Tejwant Singh fraudulently changed the number of offices in front of them.

During course of investigations, IO prepared the site plan, recorded statement of the witnesses Crl. Rev. no. 589/2017 State Vs. Manender Pal Singh Page no. 3 of 8 and seized documents concerning the case.

sentences.text:
The charge-sheet has been filed u/s.
380/406/448/120-B IPC in the present case and through the present revision the prosecution has pressed for charges u/s. 380/448/120-B IPC.
Before delving into the factual matrix of the case, let us first consider the ingredients of section 380/448 IPC.
Section 380 IPC deals theft in dwelling house, etc.

It states that "Whoever commits theft in any building, tent or vessel, which building, tent or vessel is used as a human dwelling, or used for the custody of property, shall be punished with State vs Manender Pal Singh on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178336647/
2 imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine".

entities.text: State vs Manender Pal Singh on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The points requiring proof are those necessary to prove the case of simple theft in addition to which prove:-
i.
That the property stolen was that in a building, tent or vessel.
ii. and
that the said building, tent or vessel was then used as a human-dwelling or for the custody of property.
5.1 Section 448 IPC provides punishment for house-trespass.

It states that "whoever commits house-trespass shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both".

5.2 The points requiring proof are:-
(1) That the complainant had possession of the property in question.
(2) That such property was a building, tent or vessel used as a human dwelling or any dwelling used as a place for the custody of property.
(3) That the accused entered into such building or having lawfully entered, unlawfully remained there.

(4) That he did so with intent to commit an offence or to intimidate,
insult or annoy the person in possession.
Crl. Rev. no. 589/2017 State Vs. Manender Pal Singh Page no. 4 of 8 5.3

sentences.text:
Coming to the factual matrix of the case, the prosecution has relied on the Agreement dated 30.08.1999 to show the right,
title and interest of the Complainant in office no. G-12.

Vide said agreement, respondent no. 2 transferred the right title and interest in respect of flat no. G-12 in favour of Ms. Meera Prasad and Mr. M. P. Singh representing the Ajit Singh house, Yusuf Sarai Commercial Complex Flat owner and occupants Association (hereinafter referred to as 'Association') and in that agreement, the consideration amount was shown as nil in clause no. 11 of the agreement.

entities.text: Yusuf Sarai Commercial Complex Flat owner and occupants Association
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The reason why the consideration amount was shown as nil is another agreement dated 30.08.1999 entered between respondent no. 2 and complainant Association qua which the clause was also found mention in first agreement as handwritten clause no. XX.

Perusal of the second agreement reveals that the same was entered between respondent no. 2 and the complainant wherein it was agreed that the complainant Association will provide funds for the occupation of unfinished jobs in the building such as fire fighting systems, water pumps, installation of lifts, installation of generator and installation of electrical works.
Against that agreement, respondent no. 2 agrees to give the title and possession of Flat no. G-12, Ground Floor, 12-Yusuf Sarai to the complainant association.

There is no investigation done regarding the fact whether infact the funds were provided to the respondent no. 2 in order to presume the right, title and interest of the complainant Association in the flat no. G-12.

In this regard, the Ld. Trial Court right held that "in agreement thereby flat no. G-12, measuring 209 sq. ft. was alloted by the M/s. Skipper Towers Pvt. Ltd. to the Association through Mrs. Meera Prasad and Sh. M. P. Singh, there is reference of another agreement dated 30.08.1999 in para no. 11 because no Crl. Rev. no. 589/2017 State Vs. Manender Pal Singh Page no. 5 of 8 consideration has been mentioned in para no. 11.

Instead of consideration agreement dated 30.08.1999 had been State vs Manender Pal Singh on 13 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/178336647/
3 referred.

As per agreement dated 30.08.1999 executed by Sh. Tejwant, Director of M/s Skipper Towers Pvt. Ltd. and Flat Owners and Occupants Association through its President Mrs. Meera Prasad, it was agreed that Association would provide funds to complete unfinished job in lieu of flat no. G-12 to the Association.

However, there is no evidence on record to prove that Association had actually provided the funds to the M/s Skipper Towers Pvt. Ltd. as per agreement dated 30.08.1999 to further validate allotment of flat no. G-12 to the Association.
Therefore, there was no consideration disclosed by the prosecution required for allotment of flat no. 12 of the Association".

5.4 Secondly, mere agreement is no document of possession of the immovable property and the Prosecution has not relied on any other documents apart from the said agreement to show that the comlainant Association was infact in possession of the flat no. G-12.

Thirdly, it has been alleged that it was found during investigation that treasurer Shri M.P. Singh rented out his flat bearing no. G-13 to one Shri Kamaljeet Singh in conspiracy with Shri Tejwant Singh and master Prabsaran Singh through their guardian Shri Prabjeet Singh and changed the number of office to G-12 to G-12A.

Not only that respondent no. 2 Shri Tejwant Singh fraudulently changed the number of offices in front of them however it has been nowhere said by any of the witnesses that the accused persons were seen either removing those articles or demolishing the wall between offices no. G-12 and G-13.

There is no iota of prima facie material from which it can be said that it was the accused persons who removed the alleged property out of the possession of the Association without its consent and that moving was with Crl. Rev. no. 589/2017 State Vs. Manender Pal Singh Page no. 6 of 8 dishonest intention in order to cause wrongful gain to themselves and wrongful loss to the Association.

entities.text: Crl. Rev. no. 589/2017 State Vs. Manender Pal Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Fourthly, there is no material on record from which it can be said that accused persons unlawfully entered into the office at G-13 and remained there unlawfully with intent to commit an offence.
Fifthly, no investigation was done regarding the areas of either G- 12, G-12A or G-13 which is essential in order to prima facie make out the case of criminal trespass.

In this regard, the Ld. Trial Court has rightly held that "There is no eye witness to the alleged incident of theft of articles from flat no. G-12, no recovery of those articles had been effected from possession of the accused persons.

Therefore, there is no evidence available on record to substantiate the allegations of theft of articles of the Association; that secondly, it is alleged that wall between flat no. G-12 and G-13 had been demolished.
But again there is no eye witness to the incident of demolition of said wall to prove that wall was demolished by the accused persons.
Moreover, there is no photographs of the said flats to prove any such demolition of wall.

As per the site plan prepared by IO that flat no. G- 12 and 13,
G-13A are adjoining to each other and common wall between of these two flats is shown as demolished at point-A and area of flat no. G-12 and 13, G-13A appears to be similar, however, as per the agreements placed on record the area of flat no. G-12 is 209 sq.ft., area of flat no. G-13 is 500 sq.
ft. and area of flat no. G-13A is 150 sq.ft.
The area of none of these flats is same.
Thus, the site plan prepared by the IO is not depicting the actual site.

Hence, there is no evidence on record in order to prove the allegations that accused persons had demolished the wall between flat no. G-12 and 13."
6.

In view of the aforesaid discussion and overall facts and Crl. Rev. no. 589/2017 State Vs.
Manender Pal Singh Page no. 7 of 8 circumstance of the case, I came to the conclusion that I find no infirmity or irregularity in the impugned order and revision filed by the revisionist/State is hereby dismissed.
